contract: Evaluate one pure Lua function of one plain input in a fresh PUC Lua 5.4.9 process outside the VM, started by a caller-held OTP Port from an executable that build/2 compiles from the installed pinned lua_source checkout and an owned C host, over length-framed JSON (unsigned 32-bit little-endian length, at most 1,048,576 bytes) under capability policy version 3, whose fixed allow-list of names and safe helper set (ten C helpers under the global helpers, each version 1, for JSON null and empty object, canonical JSON encode and decode, ASCII trim, plain split, UTF-8 code-point count and UTC time values that the caller passes in) has a canonical identity and refuses every other name as unlisted_name; for each declared name a function bindings.<name> is answered by the sandbox itself, as data (mode data) or as a replay of the results that the caller recorded, in order, ending at the first unrecorded call with a pending-call reply (mode replay), and a recorded call that the source does not repeat is call_mismatch; helpers charge counted steps for their work and their limits are the same sticky stops; exact positive limits on counted steps, call depth, value bytes, live Lua memory and wall time apply, and a step, depth, size or unlisted-name stop is sticky and cannot be caught or continued from Lua; input and result are plain data (null sentinel, booleans, UTF-8 strings, signed 64-bit integers, finite floats, dense arrays, string-keyed maps, at most 32 nested containers), a refusal is a fixed atom, memory, wall time, abnormal exit and protocol failure are recorded host outcomes, and the child is reaped on every return path including the death of the caller.
limits: Not OS security isolation: no container, seccomp, namespace, network or filesystem confinement; Port separation does not protect against a vulnerability in the native runtime. Policy version 3 grants the ten listed helpers and the bindings mechanism and no callbacks, clocks, random or I/O, and this Piece adds no pooling or service.

Private-layout maintenance limitation: the allocator string guard reads offsetof(TString, contents) and the string allocation tag of the pinned internal lobject.h of the lua_source checkout. The build verifies the exact upstream bytes and refuses a different revision, but a new Lua revision needs a new review of that coupling before the pin moves.

No cross-build replay claim: results of pure sources are compared across fresh calls and fresh BEAM processes of one build and one policy identity only; operators keep the pinned runtime's semantics. Memory, wall time and abnormal exit depend on allocator timing, scheduling and the operating system, so they are recorded outcomes and never replay decisions.

Tables made by table.pack carry an n key and are not dense arrays; a value_bytes limit below 4 is refused as value_size and a memory_bytes limit below the initialization baseline is a memory host outcome.

The C host assumes a Linux host: it is compiled with -DLUA_USE_LINUX and uses poll, setitimer and /dev/null. The build is not run per evaluation; the consumer owns the production build and install of the executable, and the copied-consumer test compiles into a disposable directory only.

The helpers do no Unicode normalization and no case mapping beyond the ASCII rules of string.lower and string.upper (they need Unicode data tables), and no helper reads a clock, a time zone or a locale: a time is an integer of milliseconds that the caller puts in the input, in 1970-01-01 to 9999-12-31 UTC, proleptic Gregorian.
Bindings take names only: the caller records results truthfully and the sandbox cannot tell a true result from a false one; there is no state between runs.
No caller callback, module manifest, schema check of arguments, cost, permission, recipe engine, in-VM execution or pooling.

grounding.claim: Group native_build_and_copy: a fresh build from the installed pinned checkout with plain cc and ar returns 42 from a pure function, the output directory is removed, the source checkout is not written, a missing compiler or archiver, a wrong source revision, an extra header and a failed compile refuse; negative control: none beyond the refusals. Listed scenarios pass; the same file runs in the copied consumer.

Group counted_sticky_limits: exact boundary and boundary + 1 for counted steps and call depth of known sources (chunk work included, tail calls, callbacks), string.rep, concatenation, string.pack, string.format and gsub bombs ending in value_size or the named memory outcome, value size at the cap and cap + 1, budgets below initialization, syntax error, parser and allocation failures; negative controls: an off-by-one step comparison (step boundary tests fail) and removal of the scoped allocation cap and rep pre-check (bomb tests fail). Listed scenarios pass.

Group no_catching_or_continuation: for steps, call_depth, value_size, memory, unlisted_name and wall_time, nested pcall, an error inside the handler path, repeated catches and sort and gsub callbacks never return a post-stop marker; a second stop reports the first; xpcall and coroutine are unreachable on every lookup path; a SIGSTOP'd real child and a sleeping fake end at the wall deadline independent of the instruction budget; negative control: disabling the whole sticky guard makes ten tests fail with a post-stop marker. Listed scenarios pass.

Group exact_capability_surface: the sandbox enumeration, the C-host audit of environment, libraries and string metatable, and fixed-name probes of 146 names (the ten helpers included, no bindings name) agree with the policy descriptor, whose bindings map is the three-key mechanism entry; load, require, os, io, debug, _G, _ENV, raw access, catchers, unlisted helper names such as helpers.x and helpers.json, and helper_echo end in unlisted_name directly and indirectly; tostring and string.format refuse heap identity; host-side probes of a function, pid, reference, tuple, port and atom input start no process; negative control: granting print fails the surface and audit tests. Listed scenarios pass.

Group plain_data_and_protocol: every scalar type, empty array and empty object, nesting at depth 32 and refusal at 33, byte limits at the cap and cap + 1, non-plain results, the five-key request shape and the policy checked before a process starts, malformed frames from fake executables (zero and overbound length, partial header and body, EOF, invalid JSON, duplicate keys, trailing bytes, a second reply, oversize output), a crashing child, and a synthetic private marker on stderr absent from every return value; negative control: a zero length no longer a protocol error fails the zero-length test. Listed scenarios pass.

The policy identity is canonical, the descriptor is immutable plain data holding the ten sorted helper descriptors and the bindings map, and the audit of the fresh environment equals the descriptor; negative controls: granting print and granting one more helper field fail the audit test. Listed scenarios pass.

Group policy_v3_identity: the descriptor names version 3 and the ten helpers, the identity has the prefix policy-v3:sha256: and equals the digest of the descriptor, a policy-v1: identity and an identity with one helper removed are policy_mismatch, and the audit, the descriptor and the fixed-name probes agree on the helper names (3 tests). Group helpers_surface: each listed helper is reachable, helpers.x, helpers.json, json, text, time, clock, now and helper_echo are unlisted_name also inside pcall, an assignment to helpers lasts one run, the metatable of helpers is not reachable, tostring of a helper is lua_error, null and object encode as the contract says (7 tests). Group json_round_trip: json_encode and json_decode of each scalar type, null, escapes, empty and nested containers at depth 32 with depth 33, a function, a cycle, mixed keys, a hole and a non-finite number refused in both directions as errors that pcall catches, duplicate keys, trailing bytes and invalid UTF-8 refused, canonical and round-trip texts, an input left unchanged by a decode inside the function, 1,000 calls in one run with equal results, and the output equal to the reply writer's (20 tests). Group helpers_are_bounded: a split of 65,536 separator bytes under a steps limit of 10,000, the compare work of a near-match separator, an encode over value_bytes, a decode loop near the bound ending in the memory host outcome and steps stops each end in the named sticky stop that a pcall does not continue, and the step count of each helper grows with its input on each side of a limit (10 tests). Group text_helpers: trim of each ASCII space character and of nothing else, split with a separator at the start, at the end, doubled, absent, multi-byte and empty, the code-point count of ASCII, two-, three- and four-byte characters and each invalid UTF-8 form as an error (13 tests). Group time_values: time_parts, time_unix_ms and time_iso8601 of the boundary values, the weekday of five known dates, agreement with an independent calendar on 400 spread values, inverse on 10,000 values, each value outside the range, a fraction, a missing field and an unreal date as an error, no result changed between two runs one second apart, and constant step costs (14 tests). Negative controls: granting one more helper field fails the policy and helpers audit tests, removing the charge calls of text_split, of json_encode and of json_decode each fails group helpers_are_bounded tests, and a wrong leap-year rule fails group time_values. Listed scenarios pass.

Group request_shape: each malformed calls (a missing or extra key, an unknown mode, a bad or duplicate name, 65 names, 257 records, a record whose name is not listed, names or records with mode none, records with mode data, a non-plain record) and a request without calls are invalid_request and no process starts, an argument or a result over value_bytes is value_size, 64 names and 256 records pass, the host refuses the same shapes in a raw frame, and the identity is policy-v3 while a policy-v2 identity is policy_mismatch in Elixir and in the host (12 tests). Group none_is_version_2_surface: with mode none, bindings and bindings.x are unlisted_name also inside pcall and the other modes change nothing else of the surface (2 tests). Group data_mode_builds_data: two bindings build two objects in place, null, empty object and empty array stay distinct, the arguments are a copy, 1,000 calls record nothing, bindings.unknown is unlisted_name, wrong argument counts and non-plain arguments are errors that pcall catches, an argument over value_bytes is the value_size stop, each byte of an argument and of a returned value costs one step, and an assignment to bindings lasts one run (10 tests). Group replay_in_order: no record is the pending call 0 with its name and arguments, one record the pending call 1 with the recorded result of call 0 in its arguments, two records the value, a call in the chunk is call 0, every plain result comes back as recorded (4 tests). Group replay_mismatch: another name, a changed argument, an extra key, a record list longer than the calls of the source and a record that the source did not ask for are each call_mismatch that pcall does not catch, a sort comparator and a gsub callback end the run, arguments built in another insertion order and a raw frame with the recorded keys in another order replay, an integer is not a float of the same value, an empty array and an empty object differ (8 tests). Group pending_is_sticky: a pending call inside pcall, a table.sort comparator and a string.gsub callback ends the run with the pending reply and no later marker, a steps limit reached before the call or while its argument is charged is steps, a call with a wrong argument gets no index, the first stop wins (8 tests); and the exact pending reply of the Elixir decoder, a wrong index, name or key and a pending frame outside mode replay are protocol_error (5 tests). Group same_request_same_reply: each case of the replay, data and sticky groups, with 0, 1 and 2 records and each mismatch, gives one reply in 20 fresh calls and in two fresh BEAM processes, the BEAM is alive, no child of a unique executable copy is left and a next valid call succeeds (4 tests). Group no_callback_no_state: the host audit lists no bindings name or field, fixed-name probes show bindings absent with mode none and a table of functions with data and replay, a second identical request gives the identical reply and sees nothing of the first, and a child that sends a second frame after the pending frame is protocol_error (4 tests). Negative controls: making the host calls check accept every shape fails the host shape tests of request_shape, making the Elixir mode rule accept names with mode none fails request_shape, removing the charge of the argument bytes fails the step-cost test of data_mode_builds_data, returning the recorded result without comparing the arguments fails 6 tests of replay_mismatch, and letting a pcall clear the pending stop fails 4 tests of pending_is_sticky. Listed scenarios pass.

Group replay_and_survival: 82 pure arithmetic, string, pattern, array, map, numeric-boundary, sparse-length and identity-formatting cases, each run in 20 fresh calls and in two fresh BEAM processes, return equal encoded terms or equal deterministic refusals including counted steps, depth and size; memory and wall time are recorded, not compared; a changed policy identity is refused in Elixir and in the host; after 30 adverse real-host cases, 10 fake-child cases and a wall-time stop the BEAM is alive, the OS child is reaped and a valid call succeeds; killing the caller leaves no live child; negative controls: removing the host policy comparison and removing the setitimer backstop and stdin poll fail the policy and caller-death tests. Group replay_and_survival_with_helpers: 31 pure cases that use each helper, combinations and deterministic refusals, each run in 20 fresh calls and in two fresh BEAM processes, return equal encoded terms; after 7 adverse cases with a helper (a decode memory bomb, a deep decode loop, steps and value_size stops inside pcall, invalid UTF-8, an out-of-range time and unlisted_name) the BEAM is alive, the OS child is reaped and a next helper call succeeds. Finite real-process tests; listed scenarios pass.

Relies on the pinned PUC Lua 5.4.9 checkout: the public C API, the count, call and return hooks, the lua_Alloc contract, luaL_loadbufferx text mode, the string library semantics and the private TString layout named in the limits; the build verifies the exact upstream bytes it reads.
Relies on Port semantics: open_port with spawn_executable, exit_status, environment variables unset, the link between a Port and its owner, and exit reports delivered after the child is reaped.
Relies on pinned Elixir semantics for System.cmd, Process.monitor, File and the monotonic time functions that the build and the caller-held Port owner use.
Relies on Jason 1.4.5 strict decoding with ordered objects so that duplicate keys are detected; the canonical encoder of the policy identity and the frames is the Piece's own.

The OS terminates and reaps a child on SIGKILL by its pid; the pinned numeric and build semantics (binary64, two's-complement integers, C locale at process start, the fixed hash seed and sort pivot defines) hold on the host compiler; cc, ar, kill and pgrep exist on the host; the C host runs on Linux. These are not verified by the Piece and are named so that the tests are read as finite observations.

telemetry.contract: No event, log or measurement is emitted and no observation channel carries evaluation data: the source, the input, the result and the Lua message appear only in the return value of the call that owns them. Needs: an executable built by build/2, an OS process spawn, a monotonic timer and no ambient authority.

config.contract: The five limits steps, call_depth, value_bytes, memory_bytes and wall_ms are exact positive per-call operands with inclusive maxima 1000000, 64, 65536, 16777216 and 1000 and no defaults; a missing, extra, zero, negative or oversized key is invalid_request. The policy is fixed by its identity and cannot be replaced by a request. There is no ambient Config and no hot update: a change needs a new call.

control.contract: No independent Control API: an evaluation ends by its own limits, by the wall deadline or when the caller exits, and the caller-held Port reaps the child; there is no pause, drain, cancel or pool.
